key_highlights: ASX logged a net weekly gain following an $80b US midterms relief rally, though Friday saw intraday dips and oil price declines.
Department store giant David Jones collapsed into voluntary administration after landlord talks broke down, triggering supplier contagion and retail vacancy risks.
Tech and AI infrastructure outperformed with NextDC surging, while major banks underperformed led by sharp selling in NAB.
Persistent inflation and RBA hawkishness maintain pressure on consumer discretionary, borrowing capacity, and housing valuations.

sectors.trend: Severe solvency strain culminating in David Jones entering administration and closing department stores.
sectors.implications: Heightened credit risk for retail suppliers, elevated shopping centre vacancies, and consumer down-trading.

sectors.trend: Strong upside momentum driven by global AI demand and US midterms relief.
sectors.implications: Data centre and digital infrastructure operators like NextDC command valuation premiums amidst tech tailwinds.

sectors.trend: Banking weakness led by sharp declines in NAB alongside growing concerns over housing credit capacity and mortgage risk.
sectors.implications: Compressed net interest margins and elevated provisioning risks as household borrowing limits tighten.

sectors.trend: Resilient appetite for gold, silver, and critical minerals exploration with robust broker-backed capital raisings.
sectors.implications: Speculative inflows benefit juniors and gold explorers, offsetting broader macro commodity volatility.

sectors.trend: Global crude oil sell-off juxtaposed against domestic airline operating cost pressures and flight capacity cuts.
sectors.implications: Qantas margin compression from legacy fuel contracts alongside potential downstream relief if crude weakness persists.

sectors.trend: Commercial retail tenancy instability following department store failures alongside residential price crash projections.
sectors.implications: Negative revaluation pressures on retail landlords and residential developers facing declining borrowing capacity.

key_themes: Retail insolvencies and commercial real estate tenant counterparty risk
Divergence between AI/tech infrastructure resilience and banking sector weakness
RBA macro tightness: excess demand narrative versus household mortgage stress and housing correction fears
Commodity bifurcations: gold and critical minerals exploration buoyant amidst energy volatility

risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce exposure to discretionary retail REITs; focus on non-discretionary convenience assets.
Underweight high-debt domestic retail banks; monitor bank loan impairment ratios.

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Aviation Margin Squeeze & Fuel Price Volatility
risk_assessment.mitigation: Hedge fuel input sensitivities and favour carriers with strong corporate pricing power.
Maintain cash buffers and allocate to short-duration fixed income and defensive cash generators.

opportunities.recommendation: Capitalise on digital and AI infrastructure secular tailwinds
opportunities.rationale: Data centre operators demonstrate sustained institutional demand and revenue visibility despite broader market turbulence.

opportunities.recommendation: Selectively accumulate precious metals and gold producers
opportunities.rationale: Strong institutional equity financing support and geopolitical hedge characteristics support gold exploration and production.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Trim exposure to discretionary retail landlords and major retail lenders
defensive_moves.rationale: David Jones collapse elevates tenancy default rates, rent renegotiations, and potential retail credit loss provisions.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Hedge core index exposures against domestic macroeconomic slowdown
defensive_moves.rationale: Subdued GDP growth and housing headwind risks warrant portfolio insurance on broad equities.

market_outlook.short_term: Rangebound volatility for the ASX 200 as relief from US political developments contends with domestic retail insolvency fallout and banking drag.
market_outlook.long_term: Defensive tilt recommended over 6–12 months as higher borrowing costs and weak household demand challenge earnings growth outside resource and tech sectors.
